question: Should memory-lancedb permanently expose all three recall controls, or should candidate overfetch remain an internal value derived from the public similarity and result-cap settings?
rationale: The code is technically sound, but repository policy cannot determine whether the extra configuration contract and its operational combinations are desirable permanent product surface.

options.title: Narrow the public contract
options.body: Expose recallMinScore and recallResultCap, derive a safe overfetch value internally, and retain the current live-config tests and proof.

options.title: Sponsor all three settings
options.body: Accept autoRecallOverfetch as an advanced public contract and document safe relationships between candidate count, result cap, latency, and prompt budget.

options.title: Keep fixed internal policy
options.body: Retain the current constants and close the feature unless stronger operator demand establishes a stable tuning contract.

recommendation.title: Narrow the public contract
recommendation.body: Expose recallMinScore and recallResultCap, derive a safe overfetch value internally, and retain the current live-config tests and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history introduced the closest existing memory-lancedb configuration and recall-hardening behavior.
